The AI revolution is driving an unprecedented export surge across Asia:

South Korea’s exports jumped +83.5% YoY in September, the largest annual increase on record and the strongest increase among the major Asian economies.

Furthermore, Singapore’s exports soared +46.2% YoY in August, while Malaysia and Taiwan recorded gains of +45.5% and +41.0% over the same period, respectively.

This was followed by Vietnam’s exports rising +39.1% YoY in September, while China’s exports increased +25.0% YoY in August.

Japan recorded the smallest gains, but its exports still advanced +19.3% YoY in August.

The surge was driven by strong AI-related demand, particularly for semiconductors, electronics, computers, and other technology products.

South Korea’s semiconductor shipments alone jumped +263% YoY in September.

AI demand is fueling a historic surge in Asian exports.

Institutional investors are doubling down on tech stocks:

37% of global fund managers are now overweight technology stocks, up from 30% in September, and the highest reading since August 2020, according to a BofA survey of 161 participants overseeing $453 billion in assets.

Technology also has the largest overweight positioning of all sectors.

Pharmaceuticals and Industrials follow, with 23% and 22% overweight, respectively.

On the other hand, 34% of institutional investors are underweight Consumer Discretionary, the sector's most bearish positioning since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Consumer Staples has the 2nd-most bearish positioning, with 32% of managers underweight.

Institutional investors are doubling down on tech and turning against consumer stocks.

BREAKING: The number of active home sellers in the US rose +1.2% MoM in September, or +17,276, to 1,510,784, the highest since March 2020.

At the same time, the number of active homebuyers fell -2.4%, or -23,161, to 928,892, the lowest on record.

This lifts the gap between active sellers and homebuyers to a record 581,892.

As a result, there were +62.6% more home sellers than buyers last month, the largest difference on record.

This percentage has more than doubled since November 2024.

By comparison, the 2021 low was -35.7%, when buyers outnumbered sellers by 633,854.

Hundreds of thousands of homebuyers have been priced-out.

An important note: 

The size of the candle on breakout day/breakout week is one the better signals on the validity of the breakout. 

A long daily candle or weekly candle might not be a late entry. Even though there are ways to scale in as the breakout takes place.

Type 2 breakout. https://t.co/mIW7eWqgtU
Type 4 failed breakout. You can see the issue with diagonal breakouts. Minor highs act as resistance https://t.co/mLWwzYFuGJ
Type 2 breakout. https://t.co/Dggy8M7s3e
Type 2 breakdown. https://t.co/U2Fbzpe4CN

There are several Type 1 breakouts in Global equities in a year. 

Market momentum helps to capture more of them. Capturing more Type 1 breakouts in 2-3 months period of a year depends on the cyclical nature of markets. Some of you are good in taking a break/slowing down when momentum is not there. Hats off. 

And then there are very few Type 1s and more Type 2s and Type 3 & 4s. The few Type 1s and Type 2s winnings cover the small losses of Type 3 & 4s. Treading water. Trying to stay afloat during these periods.

In the end hopefully, what you have captured during these 2-3 months period Type 1s will make the bottom line of your portfolio.

On anchoring bias: 

My go to source in information about a neighbourhood, apartment or a house is its neighbors. I go, knock on their doors and talk to them. You can get all sorts of information but don't ask their opinion on the price.

The neighbours are using old, unusually low home prices as their reference point. Because those prices are anchored in their memory, the current higher price feels excessive—even if the market has fundamentally changed.

Likewise, when a stock is breaking out to all-time highs, you don't ask an investor/trader who has been dealing with it all the time. They will tell you, it is pricey/overvalued at these levels. 

You are a fresh mind, patient and if you have done your homework, be optimistic.

Details, details, details. Everything is in the details. 

Small touches makes a huge difference.
